claims.value: Level-1C, Level-2A, and Collection 1 Level-2A
claims.note: The API also lists sentinel-2-pre-c1-l2a. Collection ids are sentinel-2-l1c, sentinel-2-l2a, sentinel-2-c1-l2a.
claims.quote: "title":"Sentinel-2 Collection 1 Level-2A"

claims.value: Cloud-optimized GeoTIFF, with JPEG 2000 assets in sentinel-2-l2a
claims.note: The sentinel-2-c1-l2a collection carries COG assets only. The sentinel-2-l2a collection carries both COG assets and -jp2 assets that point at s3://sentinel-s2-l2a.
claims.quote: The Level-1 data is the original JPEG 2000 files, and the Level-2 data includes a set of assets for the original JPEG 2000 files, as well as a set of assets for the Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) versions.
claims.locator: Sentinel-2 L1C and L2A (sentinel-2-l1c and sentinel-2-l2a)

claims.value: us-west-2
claims.note: Buckets sentinel-cogs and e84-earth-search-sentinel-data are both listed in us-west-2. One sampled Collection 1 item carries the item property storage:region us-west-2.
claims.quote: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) arn:aws:s3:::sentinel-cogs AWS Region us-west-2
claims.locator: Resources on AWS, Level 2A scenes and metadata

claims.value: Provider. Buckets are not requester pays
claims.note: The registry lists no-sign-request access for both buckets. The sampled Collection 1 item carries storage:requester_pays false. AWS states its Open Data Sponsorship Program covers storing and sharing costs.
claims.quote: AWS CLI Access (No AWS account required) aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://sentinel-cogs/
claims.locator: Resources on AWS, Level 2A scenes and metadata

claims.value: Provider. Buckets are not requester pays
claims.note: Second source for the same value. AWS states the program covers the cost of storing and sharing the dataset.
claims.quote: The AWS Open Data Sponsorship Program covers the cost of storing and sharing publicly available, high-value, cloud-optimized datasets on the Registry of Open Data on AWS .

claims.value: STAC API, SNS topics, and S3 inventory files
claims.note: SNS topic arn:aws:sns:us-west-2:608149789419:cirrus-es-prod-publish for Collection 1 and cirrus-v0-publish for the older collection. Daily parquet inventory in e84-earth-search-sentinel-data-inventory.
claims.quote: New scene notifications, can subscribe with Lambda or SQS . Message contains entire STAC record for each new Item.
claims.locator: Resources on AWS, SNS Topic entries

claims.value: STAC API, SNS topics, and S3 inventory files
claims.note: Second source. The README also lists the message attributes available for SNS filtering: collection, datetime, bbox corners, cloud_cover, and status.
claims.quote: Inventory reports are generated daily and stored as parquet files, under the `primary` configuration name
claims.locator: Sentinel-2 Collection 1 Level-2A S3 Data, Inventory Report

claims.value: December 2018 globally, April 2017 for wider Europe
claims.note: Statement covers the Sentinel-2 Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs dataset. The STAC collections sentinel-2-l2a and sentinel-2-c1-l2a both report a temporal extent starting 2015-06-27T10:25:31.456000Z, which is the Level-1C start. The registry text and the STAC extent disagree.
claims.quote: L2A data are available from April 2017 over wider Europe region and globally since December 2018.

claims.value: Yes, in the separate collection sentinel-2-c1-l2a
claims.note: The README states this collection is intended to replace sentinel-2-l2a and that reprocessing was incomplete as of April 2024. It names gaps for November 2016 to November 2019 and for 2022.
claims.quote: Items in this collection only contain assets referring to COGs of data processed to at least baseline 5.0.

claims.value: scl, cloud, and snow assets, plus aot and wvp
claims.note: Asset keys on the sampled Collection 1 item. cloud is CLD_20m and snow is SNW_20m, both 20 m uint8. scl is SCL.tif at 20 m.
claims.quote: "title":"Cloud Probabilities"

claims.value: Per-asset raster:bands scale and offset in the STAC item
claims.note: The README says a non-zero offset means the offset has not been applied to the COG. Apply the offset after the scale factor.
claims.quote: The `raster:bands` field has fields for both `scale` and `offset`.  If the `offset` is anything other than 0, then it should be applied after the scale factor to correct the data.

claims.value: Per-asset raster:bands scale and offset in the STAC item
claims.note: Observed value on the red asset of one Collection 1 item at processing baseline 05.12. Offset is non-zero, so it is not pre-applied.
claims.quote: "raster:bands":[{"nodata":0,"data_type":"uint16","spatial_resolution":10,"scale":0.0001,"offset":-0.1}]

claims.value: Usually within a few hours of Copernicus availability
claims.note: The registry gives no numeric target and no service level. Wording is qualitative.
claims.quote: New Sentinel data are added regularly, usually within few hours after they are available on Copernicus OpenHub.

claims.value: Yes. Public HTTPS COG assets need no authentication
claims.note: Supports assumption A1. Range reads of a COG return per-pixel digital numbers that the reader converts with the asset scale and offset.
claims.quote: For publicly-available assets, an `https://` URL is used since no authentication is needed.

claims.value: Global since December 2018, most antimeridian scenes excluded
claims.note: The README records the antimeridian exclusion as a known issue for sentinel-2-l1c and sentinel-2-l2a and says historical scenes will be indexed later.
claims.quote: Most of the scenes crossing the antimeridian are excluded from the Catalog.
claims.locator: Sentinel-2 L1C and L2A, Known Issues

claims.value: Free, full and open Copernicus Sentinel data terms
claims.note: The registry License section links the Copernicus Sentinel data terms and conditions. The Legal Notice grants reproduction, distribution, communication to the public, adaptation and modification, and requires the notice 'Copernicus Sentinel data [Year]'. No platform terms of use are stated on the registry page.
claims.quote: Access to Sentinel data is free, full and open for the broad Regional, National, European and International user community.

claims.value: Level-1C and Level-2A
claims.note: Buckets sentinel-s2-l1c and sentinel-s2-l2a. Zipped product buckets with a three day retention period exist for both levels.
claims.quote: Description Level 1C scenes and metadata, in Requester Pays S3 bucket

claims.value: JPEG 2000 files in the original SAFE product structure
claims.note: The COG registry entry describes the same dataset as the source of its JP2K files. The L2A readme says tile data follow the original product specification.
claims.quote: This dataset is the same as the Sentinel-2 dataset, except the JP2K files were converted into Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs (COGs).

claims.value: eu-central-1
claims.note: Both scene buckets and the L2A notification topic are in eu-central-1. The L1C notification topic is in eu-west-1.
claims.quote: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) arn:aws:s3:::sentinel-s2-l1c AWS Region eu-central-1
claims.locator: Resources on AWS, Level 1C scenes and metadata

claims.value: Requester for L1C. Registry lists L2A as no-sign-request
claims.note: The registry marks sentinel-s2-l1c, sentinel-s2-l1c-zips and sentinel-s2-l2a-zips Requester Pays. It shows sentinel-s2-l2a with a no-sign-request command. The Sinergise readme for L2A still says Requester Pays. The two pages disagree for the L2A bucket.
claims.quote: Description Level 2A scenes and metadata, in S3 bucket Resource type S3 Bucket Amazon Resource Name (ARN) arn:aws:s3:::sentinel-s2-l2a AWS Region eu-central-1 AWS CLI Access (No AWS account required) aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://sentinel-s2-l2a/
claims.locator: Resources on AWS, Level 2A scenes and metadata

claims.value: Requester for L1C. Registry lists L2A as no-sign-request
claims.note: Conflicting statement recorded beside the registry entry. The Sinergise readme for the L2A bucket states Requester Pays.
claims.quote: The data is in Requester Pays S3 bucket.

claims.value: Requester for L1C. Registry lists L2A as no-sign-request
claims.note: Definition of the charge. AWS states the requester pays request and download costs and the bucket owner pays storage. Anonymous requests are not allowed on a Requester Pays bucket.
claims.quote: With Requester Pays buckets, the requester instead of the bucket owner pays the cost of the request and the data download from the bucket.
claims.locator: Using Requester Pays general purpose buckets for storage transfers and usage

claims.value: SNS topics and S3 inventory files, plus Earth Search STAC
claims.note: SNS topics arn:aws:sns:eu-west-1:214830741341:NewSentinel2Product for L1C and arn:aws:sns:eu-central-1:214830741341:SentinelS2L2A for L2A. Inventory files in sentinel-inventory in ORC and CSV. The registry Explore links also name Earth Search and static STAC endpoints.
claims.quote: Description New scene notifications for L2A, can subscribe with Lambda or SQS . Resource type SNS Topic Amazon Resource Name (ARN) arn:aws:sns:eu-central-1:214830741341:SentinelS2L2A
claims.locator: Resources on AWS, New scene notifications for L2A

claims.value: January 2017 globally, November 2016 in Europe
claims.note: The registry Description carries the same two dates for this dataset.
claims.quote: L2A data are available in Europe from November 2016 and from January 2017 globally.

claims.value: SCL, AOT and WVP as JPEG 2000 objects
claims.note: Observed as -jp2 assets on one Earth Search sentinel-2-l2a item, which point into this bucket. The Sinergise readme does not enumerate quality layers.
claims.quote: "href":"s3://sentinel-s2-l2a/tiles/15/R/TN/2026/9/9/0/R20m/SCL.jp2"

claims.value: Usually within a few hours of Copernicus availability
claims.note: No numeric target and no service level are stated.
claims.quote: New Sentinel data are added regularly, usually within few hours after they are available on Copernicus OpenHub.

claims.value: Yes. Each file is a separate object in Amazon S3
claims.note: Supports assumption A1. A range read of a JPEG 2000 object is not equivalent to a COG range read, because JPEG 2000 codestreams need different client handling.
claims.quote: Each file is its own object in Amazon S3.

claims.value: Global for L2A from January 2017
claims.note: Tiles follow the Military Grid Reference System. Path is tiles/[UTM code]/latitude band/square/[year]/[month]/[day]/[sequence]/DATA.
claims.quote: The mission provides a global coverage of the Earth's land surface every 5 days, making the data of great use in on-going studies. L2A data are available in Europe from November 2016 and from January 2017 globally.

claims.value: 0.0043 USD per 10,000 GET requests in eu-central-1
claims.note: Amazon S3 published price for eu-central-1, SKU TUSXZSTYY6YJH244, group S3-API-Tier2, unit Requests, effective 2026-08-01, offer file version 20260831092225. Currency USD. Applies to a Requester Pays read because the requester pays the request cost. No plan or allowance is attached. Not summed with any other price.
claims.quote: $0.0043 per 10,000 GET and all other requests

claims.value: 0.02 USD per GB from EU (Germany) to US West (Oregon)
claims.note: AWS Data Transfer published price out of eu-central-1, usage type EUC1-USW2-AWS-Out-Bytes, offer file version 20260831121448. Currency USD. The same file gives the same rate to US East (Northern Virginia). Not summed with the request price.
claims.quote: $0.02 per GB - EU (Germany) data transfer to US West (Oregon)

claims.value: Free, full and open Copernicus Sentinel data terms
claims.note: The registry and the Sinergise readme both link the Copernicus Sentinel data terms. The Legal Notice requires the notice 'Copernicus Sentinel data [Year]' when data are distributed, and 'Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [Year]' when modified. AWS Requester Pays terms are a separate access condition, not a data licence.
claims.quote: EU law grants free access to Copernicus Sentinel Data and Service Information for the purpose of the following use in so far as it is lawful

claims.value: Level-1B, Level-1C, Level-2A, and Level-3 quarterly mosaics
claims.note: The documentation page carries an overview for each level. The STAC API exposes Sentinel-2 Level-1C and Level-2A collections, plus GRI L1C and Global Mosaics.
claims.quote: Sentinel-2 Level 2A Surface Reflectance Overview Sentinel-2 Level 1C Top of Atmosphere (TOA) Overview Sentinel-2 Level 1B Overview Sentinel-2 Level 3 Quarterly Mosaics

claims.value: JPEG 2000 assets in SAFE products, plus a zipped product asset
claims.note: Asset type on every band asset of the STAC collection is image/jp2. A separate Product asset of type application/zip carries the whole SAFE package.
claims.quote: "B04_10m":{"gsd":10,"type":"image/jp2"

claims.value: CloudFerro Cloud or OpenTelekom Cloud, resolver dependent
claims.note: Default endpoint https://eodata.dataspace.copernicus.eu. Users who need OpenTelekom Cloud must call https://eodata.ams.dataspace.copernicus.eu. No AWS region is offered.
claims.quote: A Global Service Load Balancer (GSLB) directs the request to either CloudFerro Cloud or OpenTelekom Cloud (OTC) S3 endpoint.

claims.value: Provider, inside free quotas. CREODIAS S3 is requester pays
claims.note: Copernicus General Users get 2000 S3 requests per minute, 4 concurrent connections, 20 MB/s per connection and a 12 TB rolling 30 day transfer limit. Above the transfer limit bandwidth drops to 1 MB/s and concurrency to 1. The STAC collection marks cdse-s3 requester_pays false and creodias-s3 requester_pays true.
claims.quote: Every user account is set a limited quota to guarantee fair sharing of free tier resources within all users of Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem.

claims.value: Provider, inside free quotas. CREODIAS S3 is requester pays
claims.note: Second source. The STAC collection declares two storage schemes with different payment rules.
claims.quote: "creodias-s3":{"type":"custom-s3","title":"CREODIAS S3","platform":"https://eodata.cloudferro.com"

claims.value: STAC API and OData catalogue, plus catalog subscriptions
claims.note: STAC endpoint https://stac.dataspace.copernicus.eu/v1/. The legacy endpoint under catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu/stac is deprecated from 17 November 2025. The documentation menu also lists Catalog subscriptions and a Traceability API.
claims.quote: It is important to note that the STAC catalogue does not replace the existing CDSE Open Data Protocol (Odata) catalogue but serves as a complementary resource, expanding data discovery and accessibility options.

claims.value: 2015-06-27T10:25:31Z per the STAC temporal extent
claims.note: This is the collection temporal extent, which starts at the mission start. The collection description says the products are Collection 1. The documentation pages do not state a separate global Level-2A start date.
claims.quote: "temporal":{"interval":[["2015-06-27T10:25:31Z",null]]}

claims.value: Collection 1 reprocessed products, archive moving to baseline 5.0
claims.note: The page says reprocessing to baseline 5.0 or better covers historical L1C and L2A up to 13 December 2023 and is near the end. The STAC collection sentinel-2-l2a describes its products as Collection 1.
claims.quote: The processing baseline indicates the version of the processing algorithm applied to the raw data to generate the Sentinel-2 products. Re-processed products are referred as Sentinel-2 Collection-1.

claims.value: Collection 1 reprocessed products, archive moving to baseline 5.0
claims.note: Second source. The STAC collection description names the product as Collection 1.
claims.quote: The Sentinel-2 Level-2A Collection 1 product provides orthorectified Surface Reflectance (Bottom-Of-Atmosphere: BOA), with sub-pixel multispectral and multitemporal registration accuracy.

claims.value: SCL, CLD, SNW, AOT and WVP assets at 20 m and 60 m
claims.note: Asset keys on one sampled item. The collection item_assets list omits CLD and SNW, but the item carries CLD_20m, CLD_60m, SNW_20m and SNW_60m.
claims.quote: "CLD_20m"

claims.value: Raw JPEG 2000 with raster:scale and raster:offset in the catalogue
claims.note: The catalogue publishes scale 0.0001 and offset -0.1 per band asset. The asset files are the original SAFE JPEG 2000 files, so the reader applies both.
claims.quote: "raster:scale":0.0001

claims.value: Raw JPEG 2000 with raster:scale and raster:offset in the catalogue
claims.note: Second half of the same asset record.
claims.quote: "raster:offset":-0.1

claims.value: PT24H, near real time, on the sampled item
claims.note: Item property product:timeliness on one item sensed and published on 2026-09-09. The item was published 2026-09-09T21:31:26Z for a 16:48:49Z sensing time. The documentation pages state no Sentinel-2 latency target. A different item may carry a different value.
claims.quote: "product:timeliness":"PT24H"

claims.value: Yes. S3 API access to EO data objects
claims.note: Supports assumption A1. Credentials come from a registered account. Each downloaded file counts as one request against the quota.
claims.quote: S3 API is one of the main access methods for EO data. It is suitable for Third Party applications that require high-performance parallel access and scalability.
claims.locator: Access to EO data via S3

claims.value: Global bounding box in the STAC collection
claims.note: Spatial extent covers the whole globe. No regional restriction is stated in the documentation.

claims.value: Copernicus Sentinel data free, full and open. Portal content non-commercial
claims.note: Data licence and platform terms are separate. The data licence is the Legal Notice on the use of Copernicus Sentinel Data. The portal terms restrict other portal content to non-commercial use and withhold the right to resell or redistribute portal material.
claims.quote: The access and use of Copernicus Sentinel data is available on a free, full and open basis through the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem and shall be governed by the Legal Notice on the use of Copernicus Sentinel Data and Service published here

claims.value: Copernicus Sentinel data free, full and open. Portal content non-commercial
claims.note: Second source, for the platform terms half of the note.
claims.quote: Any other contents of the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem portal are intended for non-commercial use.

claims.value: Level-2A
claims.note: The STAC collections listing returns 136 collections and one Sentinel-2 collection, sentinel-2-l2a. No Sentinel-2 Level-1C collection is listed.
claims.quote: This dataset contains the global Sentinel-2 archive, from 2016 to the present, processed to L2A (bottom-of-atmosphere).

claims.value: Cloud-optimized GeoTIFF
claims.note: Asset media type on every band asset is image/tiff; application=geotiff; profile=cloud-optimized. Files sit under a SAFE-shaped path in Azure Blob Storage.
claims.quote: converted to [cloud-optimized GeoTIFF](https://www.cogeo.org/) format.

claims.value: westeurope
claims.note: Storage account sentinel2l2a01, container sentinel2-l2. Asset hrefs resolve to sentinel2l2a01.blob.core.windows.net.
claims.quote: "msft:region":"westeurope"

claims.value: Provider. Data free, but assets need a SAS token
claims.note: Tokens are anonymous. Rate limiting and token expiry depend on whether the caller is inside West Europe and whether a subscription key is supplied.
claims.quote: The data hosted by the Planetary Computer is free for anyone to use.
claims.locator: Using Tokens for Data Access, first paragraph

claims.value: Provider. Data free, but assets need a SAS token
claims.note: Second source for the token half of the value.
claims.quote: The STAC metatdata API is available to all users and does not require an account or a token to use. All data assets require a token for accessing files on Azure Blob storage.

claims.value: STAC API, public and anonymous
claims.note: Endpoint https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1. No notification topic or inventory file is documented on these pages.
claims.quote: The [STAC API](../reference/stac) is public and can be accessed anonymously.

questions_answered: Which collections exist and what level and baseline does each carry? sentinel-2-l1c, sentinel-2-l2a, sentinel-2-c1-l2a and sentinel-2-pre-c1-l2a. Collection 1 items carry baseline 5.0 or later.
Which bucket and region hold the assets, and who pays? sentinel-cogs and e84-earth-search-sentinel-data, both us-west-2, neither requester pays.
How are new scenes announced? SNS topic cirrus-es-prod-publish for Collection 1, with message attributes for collection, datetime, bbox corners, cloud cover and status.
Which quality layers are delivered as assets? scl, cloud, snow, aot and wvp.
Are Collection 1 reprocessed products present? Yes, in the separate collection sentinel-2-c1-l2a.
questions_open: How far back does Level-2A coverage really go? The registry text says globally since December 2018 for this dataset, but both STAC collections report a temporal extent starting 2015-06-27. Neither page reconciles the two.
Is the reprocessing gap still open? The README records missing periods of November 2016 to November 2019 and 2022 as of April 2024. No page gives a later status.

What does a read cost? The registry states no price. The AWS Open Data Sponsorship Program page says AWS covers storing and sharing, but names no rate and no condition on the reader's region. Not settled.
Does the offset stay unapplied for every item? The README says the offset has been applied to some Items. Only two items were sampled, both with offset -0.1.
observations: One sampled Collection 1 item carried s2:processing_baseline 05.12, storage:platform AWS, storage:region us-west-2 and storage:requester_pays false.
The sentinel-2-l2a item carried both COG assets on sentinel-cogs and -jp2 assets pointing at s3://sentinel-s2-l2a, which is the requester-pays route's bucket.
The Collection 1 red asset file:size was 109709322 bytes for a 10980 by 10980 uint16 band.
The README states the API comes with no guaranteed service.
The registry entry for the GeoTIFF dataset names Element 84 under Managed By and gives opendata@element84.com as contact.
The registry lists two data buckets for this dataset, e84-earth-search-sentinel-data for Collection 1 and sentinel-cogs for the older collection.

AWS states that Requester Pays buckets do not allow anonymous requests, so every read must be authenticated.
The registry entry for the JPEG 2000 dataset also names Element 84 under Managed By, while its documentation links point to Sinergise readmes.

questions_answered: Which API returns raw pixels for a polygon? The Process API, with bands requested in DN units, which contain exactly the pixel values of the source data.

What are the processing-unit rules for small polygons? One processing unit is 512 by 512 pixels, 3 input bands, one sample per pixel, up to 16 bits per pixel. The area factor has a floor of 0.01, which is 0.25 square kilometres at 10 m. The minimum request cost is 0.005 PU for Process API and 0.01 PU for Statistical API.
Which quality layers are available? SCL, SNW, CLD, CLP, CLM, AOT and dataMask.
questions_open: What is the unit price and the subscription price? https://www.sentinel-hub.com/pricing/ redirects to https://www.planet.com/pricing/, which renders its plan table with JavaScript and returned only the heading 'Planet Pricing'. The Planet support pricing article is behind a bot check. No currency price could be quoted.
What are the retention terms? No page read states how long results or orders are retained.
Are Collection 1 reprocessed products distinguished? The L2A page describes mosaickingOrder handling of reprocessed tiles but names no Collection 1 identifier or filter.
What is the publication latency? No page read states a time from sensing to availability.
Which cloud region hosts the service? The page names the endpoint services.sentinel-hub.com and no cloud region.
observations: The documentation banner reads 'Sentinel Hub Documentation is moving to a new home at docs.planet.com . These docs will no longer be accessible.'
The Processing Unit page notes costs marked with two asterisks are not yet applied, including 200 PU per GB egressed off the platform and 20 PU per image for Orders and Subscriptions APIs.
Batch V2 and Batch Statistical APIs carry a minimum request cost of 100 PU. Asynchronous Processing API carries 10 PU.
Statistical API and Batch Statistical API return statistics rather than pixels, which is relevant to assumption A1.

The Processing Unit quotes come from the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem copy of the Sentinel Hub documentation, because docs.sentinel-hub.com/api/latest/api/overview/processing-unit/ redirects to docs.planet.com and then to a monitoring credits page.

questions_answered: Is 30 m resolution compatible with assumption A7? No. The product is 30 m by 30 m, so a 10 m water body is a fraction of one cell.
What bands and masks does it deliver? Thirteen spectral bands, four angle bands and an Fmask quality band, each as a separate COG.
What is the latency? Two to three days.
questions_open: How is the Sentinel-2 baseline 04.00 offset handled upstream? The Variables table lists scale factor 0.0001 and Offset N/A for every reflectance band, but no page read states how the L1C input offset is treated.
Are reprocessed products present, and how are they distinguished? Version 2.0 is the collection version. No page read describes reprocessing inside version 2.0.
What does direct S3 access require and cost? The assets sit in the protected bucket lp-prod-protected. Earthdata Login and temporary S3 credentials were not exercised, and no price page was read.
observations: CMR-STAC reports HLSS30_2.0 with license CC0-1.0 and a temporal start of 2015-11-28T00:00:00.000Z.
The catalog page reports 21,822,893 files or granules and processing level 3.
Reflectance bands are int16 with fill value -9999 and scale factor 0.0001. Angle bands are uint16 with fill value 40000 and scale factor 0.01.
The project page says a suite of HLS vegetation index products arrived in February 2025 and low-latency HLS products are anticipated to be completed in 2027.
Items carry both HTTPS hrefs under data.lpdaac.earthdatacloud.nasa.gov and s3:// hrefs under lp-prod-protected.

limitations: The Amazon S3 pricing page at https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/ renders its price tables from client-side placeholders such as {priceOf!s3/s3-standard!GET!...}. No number could be quoted from it. The request and data transfer prices were taken from the AWS Price List offer files for eu-central-1 instead, which are official AWS files with a stated publication date.

No currency price for Sentinel Hub could be quoted. https://www.sentinel-hub.com/pricing/ redirects to https://www.planet.com/pricing/, whose plan table is rendered with JavaScript, and the Planet support pricing article is behind a bot check. unit_price and monthly_price stay null for that candidate.

Every Microsoft Planetary Computer web page tried, including the dataset page, the docs pages and the terms page, returned only a JavaScript shell. Claims for that candidate cite the STAC API and the provider's own documentation source files in the microsoft/PlanetaryComputerDataCatalog repository.

Google Earth Engine developer guide pages under developers.google.com/earth-engine/guides also returned JavaScript shells. Only the data catalog pages, the Google Cloud pricing page and the Earth Engine terms page could be quoted. The raw pixel access claim for that route therefore rests on the pricing page's description of batch output rather than on an export guide.
LP DAAC product URLs under lpdaac.usgs.gov redirect to the NASA Earthdata site. The HLSS30 v2.0 claims cite https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/data/catalog/lpcloud-hlss30-2.0 instead.

One STAC item per collection was sampled, all over a bounding box near the Texas coast on the access date. Item-level values such as processing baseline, timeliness and asset scale or offset may differ for other items and other dates.

No image asset bytes were read. No requester-pays bucket was contacted. No credentials were used. All values come from documentation pages and from catalog and metadata endpoints that return JSON or HTML.
Prices are quoted as published. None was converted between currencies and none was summed with another.
Coverage start dates conflict between prose and STAC temporal extents for three routes. Both values are recorded, and the conflict is left open rather than resolved.

The offset_delivery field is settled for five routes and open for two: the requester-pays buckets and the Planetary Computer. Neither publishes a statement about the processing-baseline offset on any page read.

The operator of the JPEG 2000 buckets was expected to be Sinergise. Both the rendered registry entry at https://registry.opendata.aws/sentinel-2/ and its source YAML name Element 84 under ManagedBy, accessed on 2026-09-11. The pages read do not name the owner of the sentinel-s2-l1c and sentinel-s2-l2a buckets, and registry entry management is not the same as bucket ownership. Sinergise remains the publisher of the linked readmes and the contact forum.

No page read states that the sentinel-s2-l2a bucket mirrors the Copernicus archive or holds ESA SAFE packages. The source_dataset value for that route rests on the Sinergise readme's tile layout statement and the registry's Copernicus OpenHub sentence. The zipped product buckets were not examined.
